name: upstream-streaks
summary: Full-bleed dark hero on upstream-fx's WebGL streak field: hundreds of hairline streaks fan upward from a point just below the bottom edge, each fading from a dark tail to a lit head, and part in a rounded gap around the cursor, closing again right behind it. All of the motion runs on the GPU in two draw calls a frame. The canvas sits behind the section's own copy, pauses off screen and in background tabs, survives a lost WebGL context, and under reduced motion draws one still frame. With no script or no WebGL the section rests on a CSS glow in upstream's own three colours.

accentColor.description: Colour of each streak's lit head (hex or rgb()). Upstream default.

baseColor.description: Colour of each streak's dark tail. Upstream default.

background.description: Canvas clear colour behind the streaks; 'transparent' lets the section's CSS ground show through. Upstream default.

count.description: Number of streaks. Upstream default and range.

speed.description: How fast the streaks travel, in pixels per second. Upstream default and range.

length.description: Streak length in pixels. Upstream default and range.

spread.description: Half-angle of the fan, in degrees. Upstream default and range.

repelRadius.description: Radius of the gap the cursor opens, in pixels. Upstream default and range.

intensity.description: Brightness of the lit heads. Upstream default and range.

interactive.description: Whether the streaks part around the cursor. Upstream default.

deviations.what: The repo ships its plain-HTML install as the committed, minified dist/upstream.global.js; that bundle is ported verbatim inside a named function upstreamFx(e), which mount() calls once, the first time it runs. Removed: the `var Upstream=(` IIFE head, the `})({})` call, and the `$()` call that registered the <upstream-fx> custom element at load. The bundle's exports object (DEFAULT_OPTIONS, createUpstream, defineUpstreamElement) is returned instead.
deviations.why: Seam. A paw-fx module touches no global at import time, and the bundle defines a custom element the moment it loads.

deviations.what: The WebGL context is requested with failIfMajorPerformanceCaveat: true, added to upstream's getContext options. When it is refused, upstream's createUpstream returns supported: false; mount() removes its canvas and leaves the section on its CSS rest.
deviations.why: Seam. The contract asks WebGL effects to refuse a software context and fall back to the designed resting state.

deviations.what: mount(el, opts) prepends a canvas to the section, styled like the canvas in upstream's shadow root (absolute, full size, z-index -1, pointer-events none), and calls upstream's createUpstream(canvas, opts), which clamps and fills every option from DEFAULT_OPTIONS itself. update(next) is upstream's setOptions. destroy() is upstream's destroy() plus removing the canvas and data-fx-live, which is set once upstream reports a working context. Reduced motion, off-screen pause and context-loss recovery are upstream's.
deviations.why: Seam. Upstream's <upstream-fx> element is replaced by its own vanilla createUpstream function, which the README documents as the third way to use it.

deviations.what: The resting state is a CSS glow in upstream's three default colours (black ground, #03110d tail, #25d39b head) rising from below the bottom edge, where the streaks start; upstream's own no-WebGL fallback is the plain background colour. The copy sits on a blurred dark plate (--fx-scrim, a ::before with filter: blur) whose solid core covers every text box, so lit heads never pass right under the text.
deviations.why: Ours. A flat black section with nothing but a headline reads as broken before the script runs, and the lit heads are bright enough to break text contrast where they cross the copy.
